# EnterpriseGlue v0.30.0 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.29.3`.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This release contains compatibility changes that require the upgrade guidance below.

## Highlights

- **browser-evidence:** Verify the fonts used by browser evidence before bounded capture, avoiding an unused FontFaceSet stall and preserving cleanup diagnostics.
- **documentation account access:** Add a documentation-only sign-in journey and limited, revocable documentation sessions without creating a Cloud tenant.
- **package-dependencies:** Separate browser installation dependencies from optional server peers while retaining shared import paths, and correct frontend runtime dependency declarations.
- **release-authorization:** Separate local implementation, code shipping and explicitly approved multi-PR release publication, with exact generated release-document verification.
- **plugin-toolchain:** Rebuild pinned ORAS and Cosign releases with Go 1.26.9 in both installer and manager images, eliminating newly reported Go standard-library denial-of-service vulnerabilities.
- **plugin-toolchain:** Rebuild installer and manager OCI tools with patched x/net HTTP/2 modules and their required Go dependency floors.
- **release-documentation:** Generate concise and detailed batch documentation from the complete unreleased fragments and corrected evidence, retaining historical package records without repeating bumps.
- **release-preparation:** Keep an unpublished reserved release at its approved version when Release Please runs in manifest mode.
- **release-authorization:** Publish and recover one frozen release batch through signed immutable records, reviewed workflow repairs and observed registry receipts.

## User and administrator impact

- Scheduled engine-tenancy browser evidence retains its functional checks and captures the rendered fonts without waiting indefinitely for unrelated font faces.
- Documentation readers can use their existing EnterpriseGlue accounts without creating a workspace.
- Production frontend dependency audits include the workspace runtime and omit server-only installations.
- Merged code changes can accumulate in one pending release instead of automatically publishing a release after the first PR.
- Connected registry acquisition and signature verification use patched toolchain binaries.
- Connected registry acquisition and signature verification avoid the newly reported HTTP/2 SETTINGS-frame denial-of-service vulnerability.
- Release documentation omits superseded development retries and records completed source qualification.
- Replacing an unpublished candidate regenerates the approved version instead of proposing an extra minor release.
- Publication failures can resume the approved candidate without creating another software release or rebuilding its artifacts.
- Publication status distinguishes qualified, approved, publishing, partially published and verified published outcomes.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- Direct consumers of shared server modules must provide the declared optional server peers. The backend host declares them as production dependencies. Browser schema, authorization catalog, and contract consumers need no database, mail, or HTTP server dependencies.
- Set RELEASE_AUTOPILOT_ENABLED=false, reinstall the maintained workflow plugin, and use /release to publish the complete agreed batch through the explicit source/tag/PR dispatch.
- Upgrade installer and manager images and their version-matched Helm charts as one verified toolchain set; retain existing signature, digest and disconnected-import requirements.
- Upgrade installer and manager images with their version-matched charts as one qualified set.
- Use explicit replacement preparation after the corrected protected-main helper is merged.
- Install workflow plugin 0.1.16 and the reviewed protected-main publication workflows; use the frozen source and explicit recovery_prs when repairing an already qualified release.

## API and integration compatibility

- Add public documentation-origin configuration plus dedicated documentation grant, exchange, session-verification and sign-out endpoints.
- Shared server imports keep their paths and signatures but now require optional peer dependencies supplied by the server consumer.

## Configuration

- The pinned Playwright screenshot font-ready switch is scoped to the owned capture after explicit used-font verification, and restored immediately.
- Set EG_DOCUMENTATION_ORIGIN and an API-only EG_DOCUMENTATION_GATEWAY_SECRET matching the documentation gateway; unset configuration disables the integration.
- pnpm-workspace.yaml is the single override authority; the inactive npm-style root overrides are removed.
- Release Please push and schedule runs prepare release PRs without tagging. Publication dispatch requires publish_release=true, source_ref, release_tag, release_pr and required_prs.
- The workflow plugin advances independently to 0.1.15; /new-change stops locally and /ship excludes Release Please PRs.
- Legacy release-autopilot and hotfix auto-merge inputs are retained but cannot authorize a release.
- Release-control CI includes a five-minute read-only authorization canary, required by ci-complete; it creates no public tags, packages or images.
- Both toolchain image builds use the immutable multi-architecture Go 1.26.9 Alpine builder digest. ORAS 1.3.4 and Cosign 3.1.3 module versions remain pinned; later module-specific security remediation is recorded separately.
- Both ORAS and Cosign resolve golang.org/x/net 0.60.0, x/crypto 0.57.0 and x/text 0.42.0 and x/mod 0.41.0. The pinned Go 1.26.9 builder and upstream OCI tool releases remain unchanged.
- The preparation helper applies a managed Release-As commit override to the newest reviewed first-party code PR contained in the source. The pinned action ignores its release-as input in manifest mode.
- Only labels actually attached to the old reservation are removed; missing legacy label definitions are tolerated.
- Explicit release dispatch retains source_ref, release_tag, release_pr and required_prs; optional recovery_prs lists every reviewed publication-only repair after the frozen source.
- Signed publication identities and append-only observations are stored in enterpriseglue-oss-release-publication on GHCR.
- Release Publication Reconcile automatically observes publisher completion. Manual resume=true renews approval and security acceptance before dispatching only incomplete publishers.
- GitHub history reads project merge state, branch names and labels one bounded page at a time; the workflow plugin advances independently to 0.1.16.
- Explicit prepare_replacement=true may supersede an unpublished reserved release PR and regenerate one replacement candidate at the same version. Neither tag nor GitHub release may exist.

## Database migrations

- A bounded pending handoff identifier and at most four active documentation-token identifiers are stored in existing refresh-session metadata; no tenant rows or provisioning events are written.
- Database drivers remain production dependencies of the backend host; no schema change.
- No database or application schema change.
- No application, database or published-package change.
- No database or application-runtime changes.
- Database rollback supported for the combined release: yes.

## Security

- All engine-tenancy and authorization assertions remain mandatory; missing or failed rendered fonts fail capture.
- Short-lived PKCE-bound single-use grants and audience-separated documentation tokens retain live account and source-session revocation checks. Recovery credentials cannot create documentation grants.
- DOMPurify floor moves from ^3.4.12 (locked 3.4.14) to ^3.4.16 to address GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p.
- Server dependency versions remain on their already approved release lines.
- Automatic events, labels and autopilot settings cannot authorize production tag creation. Publication requires an exact protected source, merged batch ancestry, generated document and managed-comment equality, and the existing signed candidate proof.
- Go 1.26.9 fixes CVE-2026-78667 (net/http range-header CPU exhaustion; https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6609) and CVE-2026-97031 (crypto/tls ECH memory amplification; https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6607). The patched standard library is compiled into ORAS and Cosign in both images.
- Scanner severity and ignore policy are unchanged. No exception or ignore-unfixed flag is introduced.
- Fix CVE-2026-78669 / GO-2026-6611 in golang.org/x/net/http2; Go 1.26.9 alone only fixes the separate standard-library implementation. The Go advisory identifies x/net 0.60.0 as fixed.
- Scanner severity and ignore policy remain unchanged.
- Only package entries identical to the comparison baseline are retained as historical evidence. Fresh source changes and altered package transitions still require valid version bumps.
- Replacement still requires an explicit protected-main dispatch and verified absence of both semantic tag and GitHub release. Publication and all candidate acceptance gates remain separate.
- Generated release PR bodies and existing human commit overrides are not rewritten by the preparation helper.
- Automatic events remain non-publishing. Frozen batch ancestry, generated-document and managed-comment equality, exact candidate signatures and immutable payload hashes remain mandatory.
- Recovery requires explicit first-party repair PRs and a strict path allowlist. Application sources, dependency locks, package manifests, Dockerfiles, charts, migrations, scanner policy and unknown paths cannot qualify as publication-only repairs.
- Fresh scans cover all five exact image roles on AMD64 and ARM64 under the pinned scanner and unchanged severity/ignore policy, with current vulnerability database metadata and hashed reports.
- Unknown registry state and immutable conflicts stop recovery writes. Scratch canary records are marked as fixtures and cannot enter the production publication repository.

## Known limitations

- This repairs the observed screenshot FontFaceSet stall, not a guarantee against every future CI failure.
- Gateway routing and secrets must be deployed together before enabling the public documentation hostname.
- The new flow is disabled without explicit gateway configuration. The gateway and hostname have not been deployed; real-provider/staging acceptance remains required.
- A frontend dependency graph is not a substitute for inspecting the built browser bundle.
- The release merge/publication interval is frozen; a change to protected main invalidates the approved source and stops publication.
- Exact dual-architecture image scans, signing, immutable repull and disconnected-import rehearsal remain required before publication.
- Current dual-architecture scans and signed candidate qualification remain required before publication.
- Source-level evidence cannot establish final combined candidate or production publication acceptance.
- Only unpublished reserved versions may be replaced. The replacement still needs generated-document agreement and exact signed candidate acceptance.
- Observed registry publication does not establish Cloud installation, route promotion or production deployment.
- A content change requires a new generated document and qualified candidate; only reviewed publication-only repairs may reuse frozen artifacts.

## Rollback

- Revert the evidence helper and restore Playwright default screenshot preparation.
- Disable the documentation origin and gateway deployment. Existing account and organization flows remain independently available.
- Restore the previous package versions and lockfile; no database rollback is needed.
- Restore the prior workflow only through an explicitly authorized change; do not alter published tags or bypass candidate validation.
- Do not restore vulnerable Go binaries. If operational rollback is necessary, use a previously qualified patched toolchain set; no database rollback is needed.
- Do not restore vulnerable embedded modules; use an independently qualified patched toolchain set or suspend affected connected acquisition. No database rollback is required.
- Revert the guard correction and documentation changes; no package or database rollback is required.
- Stop replacement dispatches and revert the preparation helper if required. Retain existing releases and signed records; no database or package rollback is needed.
- Revert the reviewed publication tooling and stop new recovery dispatches. Retain signed records and existing releases; never delete or repoint published tags. No package or database rollback is required.
